MERIDIAN CAPITAL PARTNERS — ANNUAL PORTFOLIO REVIEW REPORT
Fiscal Year 2024 | Prepared by: Investment Committee
Date: December 31, 2024
Confidential — For Internal Use Only

=============================================================================
INVESTMENT COMMITTEE MEMBERS
=============================================================================

  Robert Ashworth    — Managing Partner, Chair of Investment Committee
  Priscilla Fontaine — General Partner, Growth Equity Lead
  Kweku Mensah       — General Partner, Infrastructure and Climate Lead
  Yuki Tanaka        — Partner, Technology Sector Lead
  Diana Ostrowski    — Partner, Consumer and Healthcare Lead
  Alejandro Torres   — CFO, Financial Reporting
  Sophie Leclercq    — Head of ESG and Impact Measurement
  Tomasz Kowalczyk   — Chief Risk Officer

=============================================================================
PART 1: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
=============================================================================

Meridian Capital Partners closed Fiscal Year 2024 with $4.2 billion in assets
under management across three active funds: Meridian Growth Fund IV, Meridian
Infrastructure Fund II, and Meridian Climate Opportunities Fund I.

The portfolio delivered a net IRR of 18.4% for Growth Fund IV, outperforming
the Cambridge Associates Global Venture benchmark (14.1%) by 430 basis points.
Infrastructure Fund II delivered a net IRR of 11.2%, in line with expectations
for the asset class.  Climate Opportunities Fund I, in its second year of
deployment, reported a 22.7% unrealised return on invested capital.

Robert Ashworth opened the annual review by noting that 2024 was a year of
significant portfolio maturation.  Seven portfolio companies achieved major
milestones: two completed IPOs (Vortex Analytics on Nasdaq, QuantumHealth on
NYSE), three completed strategic acquisitions, and two are now profitable with
positive free cash flow.

The committee voted unanimously to proceed with fundraising for Meridian Growth
Fund V, targeting $1.5 billion in commitments, to begin in Q2 2025.

=============================================================================
PART 2: GROWTH FUND IV PORTFOLIO REVIEW
=============================================================================

2.1 Fund Overview

Vintage Year: 2019
Total Commitments: $875 million
Capital Called: $743 million (85%)
Distributions to Date: $214 million
Current NAV: $1.31 billion
Net IRR: 18.4%
Net MOIC: 2.1x

2.2 Portfolio Company Updates

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Company: Vortex Analytics
Sector: Enterprise SaaS
Lead Partner: Yuki Tanaka
Status: PUBLIC (IPO: March 2024, Nasdaq: VRTX)

Vortex Analytics completed its IPO in March 2024 at $28 per share, valuing the
company at $1.1 billion.  Meridian's holding was partially distributed to LPs
at IPO; the retained position is subject to a 90-day lockup that expired in
June.  The company's ARR at IPO was $142 million with 118% net dollar retention.
Yuki Tanaka represented Meridian on the board from 2020 through IPO.

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Company: QuantumHealth
Sector: Healthcare Technology
Lead Partner: Diana Ostrowski
Status: PUBLIC (IPO: September 2024, NYSE: QMHC)

QuantumHealth provides AI-powered diagnostic imaging tools for radiology
departments.  Its NYSE listing in September 2024 was oversubscribed 4.2x.
Market cap at IPO: $2.4 billion.  Meridian invested $65 million across three
rounds (Series A, B, and C) and realised an approximate 9x return on invested
capital at the IPO price.  Diana Ostrowski served as board observer from 2021.

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Company: NovaBridge Logistics
Sector: Supply Chain Technology
Lead Partner: Priscilla Fontaine
Status: ACQUIRED (Acquirer: GlobalFreight Corp, November 2024)

NovaBridge was acquired by GlobalFreight Corp for $340 million.  Meridian
invested $42 million at Series B.  The acquisition generated a 3.8x gross
return.  Priscilla Fontaine notes that the integration thesis — connecting
mid-market manufacturers with last-mile delivery networks — proved correct,
with NovaBridge's GMV growing 4x during Meridian's holding period.

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Company: Arboreal Carbon
Sector: Climate Tech / Carbon Markets
Lead Partner: Kweku Mensah
Status: ACTIVE — Series C (closed Q3 2024, $120M round)

Arboreal Carbon operates verified reforestation projects across Southeast Asia
and Central Africa.  The Series C was led by BlackRock's Climate Infrastructure
fund with Meridian participating for $28 million.  ARR from carbon credit sales:
$67 million.  Kweku Mensah serves as a board director.  Sophie Leclercq has
tracked Arboreal's ESG metrics, which include 2.4 million tonnes of CO2
sequestered to date.

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Company: Sentinel Cybersecurity
Sector: Enterprise Security
Lead Partner: Yuki Tanaka
Status: ACTIVE — Series B

Sentinel provides zero-trust network access for distributed enterprise teams.
ARR: $38 million (up from $14 million in 2023).  NRR: 131%.  The company is
on track for Series C in H1 2025.  Yuki Tanaka sits on the board.  The
company's key product differentiator is a proprietary identity graph that
detects lateral movement attacks with 99.4% precision.

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Company: RoboForm Automation
Sector: Industrial Robotics
Lead Partner: Priscilla Fontaine
Status: ACTIVE — Series A (struggling)

RoboForm has experienced headwinds due to a global slowdown in manufacturing
capex.  Revenue is flat at $8 million.  Priscilla Fontaine is working with
management on a cost restructuring.  A bridge financing of $5 million was
approved by the Investment Committee in October 2024.  Tomasz Kowalczyk has
flagged RoboForm as a watch-list company in the risk register.

=============================================================================
PART 3: INFRASTRUCTURE FUND II PORTFOLIO REVIEW
=============================================================================

3.1 Fund Overview

Vintage Year: 2021
Total Commitments: $1.2 billion
Capital Called: $890 million (74%)
Distributions to Date: $87 million
Current NAV: $1.14 billion
Net IRR: 11.2%

3.2 Portfolio Company Updates

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Company: PeakGrid Energy
Sector: Grid-Scale Battery Storage
Lead Partner: Kweku Mensah
Status: ACTIVE — operational

PeakGrid operates 14 battery energy storage systems (BESS) across the ERCOT
and CAISO markets.  Total installed capacity: 1.2 GWh.  Revenue in 2024: $94
million from capacity auctions and energy arbitrage.  Kweku Mensah leads the
board sub-committee on energy market policy.

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Company: UrbanFiber Networks
Sector: Fiber Broadband Infrastructure
Lead Partner: Alejandro Torres (financial observer)
Status: ACTIVE — construction phase

UrbanFiber is building fiber-to-the-premises networks in Tier 2 and Tier 3
cities across the American Midwest.  14,000 homes passed in 2024; target is
50,000 by end of 2025.  The project is financed with a combination of Meridian
equity and $310 million in project finance debt arranged by JPMorgan.

=============================================================================
PART 4: CLIMATE OPPORTUNITIES FUND I
=============================================================================

4.1 Fund Overview

Vintage Year: 2023
Total Commitments: $650 million
Capital Called: $285 million (44%)
Current NAV: $350 million
Unrealised Return on Invested Capital: 22.7%

Sophie Leclercq leads ESG measurement for this fund.  All portfolio companies
are required to report quarterly to the UN Sustainable Development Goals
framework and the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD).

=============================================================================
PART 5: KEY DECISIONS MADE BY THE INVESTMENT COMMITTEE IN FY2024
=============================================================================

DECISION 1: Approve QuantumHealth follow-on (Series C)
  Decided by: Diana Ostrowski, ratified by full committee.
  Rationale: Strong unit economics, clear path to IPO within 18 months.
  Amount committed: $22 million.

DECISION 2: Approve bridge financing for RoboForm Automation
  Decided by: Priscilla Fontaine, with approval from Tomasz Kowalczyk.
  Rationale: Management restructuring plan credible; liquidation value exceeds
  bridge amount.  Amount: $5 million.

DECISION 3: Launch fundraising for Meridian Growth Fund V
  Decided by: Robert Ashworth (unanimous committee vote).
  Target: $1.5 billion. Anchor LP commitments expected from existing LPs.

DECISION 4: Initiate ESG scorecard standardisation across all funds
  Decided by: Sophie Leclercq with Robert Ashworth sign-off.
  Rationale: Regulatory requirements under SFDR Article 9 require standardised
  reporting by Q2 2025.

=============================================================================
PART 6: RISK REGISTER SUMMARY
=============================================================================

Tomasz Kowalczyk presented the following risk items to the committee:

HIGH RISK:
  - RoboForm Automation: revenue stagnation, potential total loss scenario.
  - UrbanFiber construction delays due to permitting backlog in Ohio.

MEDIUM RISK:
  - Sentinel Cybersecurity: competitive pressure from CrowdStrike expansion.
  - Currency risk in Climate Fund I (holdings denominated in EUR and BRL).

LOW RISK:
  - Vortex Analytics lockup expiry overhang resolved in Q3 2024.
  - PeakGrid regulatory risk in ERCOT reduced after PUCT ruling in August.

=============================================================================
PART 7: 2025 OUTLOOK AND PRIORITIES
=============================================================================

Robert Ashworth outlined three strategic priorities for 2025:

1. Complete fundraising for Meridian Growth Fund V by Q4 2025.
   Owner: Robert Ashworth and Alejandro Torres.

2. Execute planned exits: Sentinel Cybersecurity (Series C → IPO track) and
   Arboreal Carbon (secondary sale of Meridian stake at 4x target).
   Owner: Yuki Tanaka (Sentinel), Kweku Mensah (Arboreal).

3. Deploy remaining $365 million in Infrastructure Fund II into two new
   infrastructure assets identified in pipeline (fiber and green hydrogen).
   Owner: Kweku Mensah with support from Alejandro Torres.

=============================================================================
END OF REPORT
Prepared by: Alejandro Torres, CFO, Meridian Capital Partners
Reviewed by: Robert Ashworth, Managing Partner
Next Review: June 30, 2025
